summary: Key inherited maye mčaple to explicit Detransitive sense 1.
rationale: The box already establishes its participial treatment; this adds a sense key without changing text.
Explicit gloss for the already present Detransitive Part. Pass. box and inherited maye mčaple; no new stem or form claimed.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (PrS 52/57)

data.turoyo: I ḥḏo ʕayno am mayayḏa kməštən, w i ḥḏo mčaple ne.
data.translation: eine mit trinkbarem und eine mit schlechtem Wasser.

rationale: Thin existing Detransitive Part. Pass. cell; predicated water quality in a contrast between two springs.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (PrS 52/58)

data.turoyo: Ummo: "Alo, lə kmašəġanne bam maye d kməštən, gmašġanne ba mčaple."
data.translation: "Bei Gott!" sprach sie, "nicht will ich sie in diesem Wasser, das getrunken wird, waschen, sondern lieber in dem schlechten."

rationale: Thin existing Detransitive Part. Pass. cell; substantivised mčaple with washing context.

summary: No new Part. Pass. box is required: inherited maye mčaple already occupies this Detransitive box. The two new contexts provide predication and substantivisation, not evidence for separate lexical meanings.
The inherited section lacked an explicit Detransitive sense list, so sense 1 is supplied for its existing state meaning and the old example receives that key.

Active Infectum at 4/41 has smoke as an inanimate causer and air as affected object. The supplied water examples present a state without an expressed agent; they do not establish a finite Detransitive paradigm.

The edition calls the water schlecht. Turoyo mčaple and the inherited example support dirty water, without a separate spoiled-water, poisonous-water or moral sense. The etymology is retained verbatim.
The German at PrS 52/57 is only a noun-phrase fragment. Confirm full verse boundaries if a complete edition sentence is wanted; no extra translation has been supplied.
